subject: Evidence export & SIEM integration for FinCo private deployment
messages:
From: Danielle Park <danielle.park@finco.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: security@finco.com, ops@finco.com
Date: Fri, 02 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence export & SIEM integration for FinCo private deployment

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for walking through the private deployment options yesterday. Our security and ops teams want to lock down the evidence export plan for the on-prem rollout. Specifically we need to confirm: 

- Supported export delivery targets (Splunk HEC, S3-compatible endpoints, syslog)
- Transport security (mTLS, cipher baseline, client cert rotation cadence)
- Minimal network rules (IP allowlist, outbound port requirements)
- Retention & chain-of-custody notes for incident response

I've attached a short checklist and some sample logs. Can you and your team confirm what we should expect from Redwood for the initial handoff and what artifacts you'll provide?

We'd like to schedule a 30-minute call next week to finalize the handshake.

Thanks,
Danielle
Danielle Park
Director, Security Engineering
FinCo Financial Services
From: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Park <danielle.park@finco.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 02 Jun 2028 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Evidence export & SIEM integration for FinCo private deployment

Danielle — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers inline and then a proposal for next steps.

- Delivery targets: Redwood Private supports Splunk HEC (TLS/HEC token), S3-compatible endpoints (presigned URL or VPC egress to S3), and raw syslog/tcp with optional TLS.
- Transport security: We recommend mTLS for syslog/Splunk HEC over private links; our standard cipher baseline is TLS1.3 with AEAD ciphers. We can also support HEC token-only setups if mTLS is not allowed.
- Network rules: Outbound to your collector's IP range on 443 (HEC) or 6514 (syslog-TLS) depending on the target; for S3 flows we need HTTPS 443 to your S3 endpoint(s). We provide a minimal list of CIDR blocks and FQDNs for allowlisting.
- Retention/chain-of-custody: We will produce an evidence bundle (signed manifest) and keep a transient staging buffer for X hours (configurable) before delivery; we do not persist customer logs in hosted storage for private deployments beyond the staging window.

Attachments: we are sending a recommended shipper config (evidence-shipper-config.yaml), the sample logs you can use for schema mapping, and our outbound checklist (finco-siem-checklist.pdf).

Proposed next steps:
1) Internal handoff doc from Redwood with exact IPs/FQDNs and TLS fingerprint (action: Kimberly)
2) Joint validation run with FinCo test collector using the sample logs (action: Marissa)
3) Finalize SLOs for delivery & failure retry behavior (action: Tessa)

Can we do Tuesday 10:00–10:30 PT for the call? If that works, we'll send an invite and a short runbook for the validation.

— Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, Danielle Park <danielle.park@finco.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 02 Jun 2028 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Evidence export & SIEM integration for FinCo private deployment

Danielle,

Following up with the concrete network/FQDN details you asked for. Below is the minimal allowlist we need for the outbound exporter that will run in the FinCo VPC (we'll provide a Terraform snippet in the runbook):

- Destination: shipper-finco.redwood-inference.net (TLS, port 443) — for S3-native transfers (we'll exchange presigned URLs).
- Destination: hec-collector-1.finco.internal (HEC, port 443) — public IPs: 198.51.100.23/32, 198.51.100.24/32 (we will provision these in the validation stage).
- Destination: syslog-collector.finco.internal (syslog-TLS, port 6514) — note: if you require mTLS, we'll provide client certs and CA chain.

Cipher baseline: TLSv1.3 (TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384), RSA not used for data path. Cert rotation: client cert TTL 90 days by default; we can extend to 180 with an approval.

I'll attach a short Terraform snippet and the HEC header example in the runbook before the call.

Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Security Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Danielle Park <danielle.park@finco.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: security@finco.com, ops@finco.com
Date: Fri, 02 Jun 2028 12:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Evidence export & SIEM integration for FinCo private deployment

Thanks Kimberly — this is helpful. Two quick clarifications from our side before the call:

1) For HEC we prefer mTLS + token. Will Redwood attach a client cert at the exporter level and allow us to terminate TLS on our collector?
2) For S3 presigned flows: can we enforce object encryption at rest on our side (SSE-S3 / SSE-KMS) and will Redwood sign the presigned URLs instead of holding any long-term creds?

If those are possible, Tuesday 10:00 PT works for us. Please send the calendar invite and include any short prep notes.

Danielle
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Park <danielle.park@finco.com>
Cc: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 02 Jun 2028 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Evidence export & SIEM integration for FinCo private deployment

Danielle — short answers and what we'll bring to the validation run: 

1) HEC/mTLS + token: Yes. The exporter will present a client cert (mTLS) and include the HEC token header. You can terminate TLS on your collector; we will provide the client cert and CA chain. We'll also show you how to rotate the certs during the validation.

2) S3 presigned & encryption: Yes. Redwood will generate presigned PUT URLs for objects and we do not hold long-term S3 credentials. You can enforce SSE-KMS on the bucket; the presigned URL flow will include the necessary headers for server-side encryption. We'll document the exact header behavior in the runbook.

Validation run plan (we'll run this during the 30-min call):
- Step 1: Confirm TLS handshake and client cert is accepted by FinCo collector
- Step 2: Push 3 sample ndjson files (attached) to your HEC and S3 test endpoints
- Step 3: Confirm event parsing in FinCo SIEM; exchange snippets for field-mapping issues

I'll send the calendar invite for Tue 10:00 PT and attach the Terraform snippet and runbook checklist.

Cheers,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Platform Engineering, Redwood Inference
